data.title: Theocritus

thumbnail.alt_text: A work made of oil on canvas.

data.inscriptions: Inscribed lower right: J. C. Cazin
data.publication_history:
T. Child, "Some Modern French Painters," Harper's Monthly 80 (1890): 829; reprinted in American Art Galleries Catalogue (1893): 10.

Paul Desjardins, "En Memoire de Jean-Charles Cazin," Gazette des Beaux-Arts 26, per. 3 (1901): (ill. opp. p. 182_.

Frank Gibson, Six French Artists of the Nineteenth Cantury (London: Robert Scott, 1925), 52.

Richard R. Brettell, French Salon Artists, 1800–1900 (Chicago: Art Institute of Chicago; New York: H.N. Abrams, 1987), 180, 109 (ill.),, 117 as c. 1885/90.

Richard Thomson, "Jean-Charles Cazin, 1881–83: Naturalism and Networking, Regionalism and Republicanism," Burlington Magazine 166 (Mar. 2024): 281 fig. 3, 284.
data.exhibition_history:
New York, American Art Galleries, Paintings by Jean Charles Cazin, 1893, cat. 95.

Art Institute of Chicago, Paintings from the Collection of Mrs. Potter Palmer, 1910, cat. 6, as Theocrite.

Art Institute of Chicago, A Century of Progress: Exhibition of Paintings and Sculpture, June 1–Nov. 1, 1934, cat. 158.

Tokyo, The Seibu Museum of Art, The Impressionist Tradition: Masterpieces From The Art Institute of Chicago, Oct. 18–Dec. 17, 1985, cat. 51; Japan, Fukuoka Art Museum, Jan. 5–Feb. 2, 1986; Japan, Kyoto Municipal Museum of Art, Mar. 4–Apr. 13, 1986.
data.provenance_text: M. E. May collection; sold, Georges Petit, Paris, June 4, 1890, lot 9. Durand-Ruel, New York; sold to Potter Palmer (1870–1902) and Bertha  Palmer (1849–1918; born Bertha Honoré), Chicago, Nov. 23, 1894 [Durand-Ruel sales records, stock number 1078; copy in curatorial file]; bequeathed to the Art Institute, 1922.
